text:
maya: Heads up — noticed a canary that kept autopause twice in a row during yesterday's traffic spike. Looks like cost guard fired, then latency guard fired a few minutes later and both paused. Anyone seen the chain-reaction?

sam: ugh. saw similar on beta-tenant. telemetry lag + guard overlap probably. did the console show two separate pause events?

maya: yep. UI showed 'autopause: cost' at 15:23, then 'autopause: latency' at 15:27. But traffic was already routed away after first pause, so second pause was noisy.

oliver: that suggests guards aren't marking 'already-paused' state across policy decisions. they each run independently on the stream of metrics.

judy: what's the current guard evaluation window?

maya: 1m for cost burn-rate, 30s for p95 latency. both use raw metric feed from prometheus with ~20s scrape latency.

sam: suggestion: add a short circuit state that is set when any autopause triggers, with TTL ~2m. other guards check that state before taking pause action. simple debounce.

oliver: agreed. also consider making pause actions idempotent: if route is already held, additional pause events should be logged but not create new incidents/notifications.

maya: debouncing helps, but we still have a problem when two different thresholds should trigger different remedial actions (e.g., cost => reduce split to 0.2, latency => full pause). we don't want to swallow the stronger action.

sam: true. propose priority levels on guard outcomes. each guard returns {severity: low|high, action: divert|reduce|pause}. executor picks highest severity within TTL window. if a low-priority already set but a high-priority arrives within TTL, upgrade.

judy: nice. we can implement priority as integer in guard config. UI needs to expose priority and TTL fields. How will this look in config yaml?

maya: quick example:

```
guard:
  name: token-burn-rate
  window: 60s
  threshold: 0.8
  action:
    type: reduce_split
    target: 0.2
  priority: 10
  ttl: 120s

---
guard:
  name: p95-latency
  window: 30s
  threshold_ms: 350
  action:
    type: pause
  priority: 50
  ttl: 180s
```

oliver: executor pseudo: if state.exists and incoming.priority <= state.priority => log & noop. else apply incoming.action and set state = incoming with ttl.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: rollout/service-alpha v2 -> canary split 10% -> 2245123400

infra-monitor: FYI, prometheus scrape lag improved after infra change at 16:00. earlier spike had 20-25s lag.

maya: next steps: (1) implement short-circuit state/key in control plane; (2) add priority + ttl to guard API; (3) console shows combined guard wall with most-severe current decision and an action history condensed to avoid duplicate noise.

sam: I'll draft the API patch and minimal executor changes. aiming for a small experiment behind feature flag. :thumbsup: \n
judy: UX: add a tooltip explaining why a low-priority earlier action didn't apply if superseded.

maya: ok thanks. filing follow-ups: ENG-1029 (executor priority) and ENG-1030 (console duplicate suppression). tagging @oncall for visibility.

oliver: sounds good. if anyone wants to prototype the state design ping me.

maya: thanks all. closing thread. :v:
